article.title: Mobile Storefront Filters: A Practical Guide to Safe, Reversible Choices
article.thesis: Mobile filters work best when customers can see what is active, operate each control reliably, and undo a narrowing decision without losing their browsing context.
article.audience_search_intent: How should a storefront design mobile product filters so customers can narrow results without losing their place?

deduplication.reason: This guide addresses mobile filter state, recovery, and interaction patterns; it does not duplicate the recent size-guide or quote-form guides.

sources.evidence: W3C explains the 24 by 24 CSS pixel target-size criterion and its spacing exceptions.
W3C describes modal-dialog focus containment and inert content outside an active dialog.
W3C provides the disclosure pattern used to distinguish a smaller in-page filter group from a modal task.

validation.runner_result: initial schema failure was corrected; a second Windows runner hung after its lint child exited and did not write a report

sequential_equivalent_gate.evidence: new prerendered route produced; Windows npm parent did not terminate after children completed

limits: No analytics, search-console, Bing Webmaster, customer outcome, or conversion evidence was available for this editorial run.
The guide is a framework and worked example, not a claim of conformance or measured storefront performance.
Commit, CI, deployment, and production verification remain pending at receipt creation.
